rationale: Structure is organized but topic_map timestamps are null. Faithfulness is low: candidate invents CVE-2026-22812, 'The Homer' comparison, 40k pruning, GitHub auto-close action, /btw 5-minute extension, Ouroboros review agent, 1.5M lines graph, Microsoft CTO 95%, and several unsupported quotes ('Our product has been 100% built by agents...'). Coverage omits good-task properties (scoped, closed loop, boring, reproduction, rubber ducking) and key stats (5,000 issues/PRs, 90% garbage, 2-week enterprise complexity). Precision suffers from non-verbatim/timestamp-mismatched quotes and wrong numbers. Compression is poor due redundant restatement across overview, topic_map, key_points, takeaways, and compressed.
hallucinations: Claude Code evolving into a complex tool with unnecessary features is compared to 'The Homer' car from The Simpsons.
OpenCode had a vulnerability (CVE-2026-22812) where its server started with default CORS headers that allowed any website to access it.
OpenCode's practice of pruning tool outputs after 40k tokens is cited as a way it 'lobotomizes the model'.
The speaker implemented a GitHub action that auto-closes pull requests and requires the user to first create a well-described issue in their 'human voice' to filter out automated 'clankers'.
A user created a `/btw` (by the way) command extension for pi in 5 minutes, demonstrating its rapid extensibility.

A graph illustrating that an agent swarm can generate over 1.5 million lines of code in two days, with a corresponding explosion in the number of cumulative errors compared to a single agent or a human.
The idea of using a 'review agent' to check the code of a 'developer agent' is dismissed as an 'Ouroboros' loop that doesn't solve the core quality problem.
Microsoft's CTO expects 95% of all code to be AI-generated by 2030.
Your context is not your context. Claude Code is the thing that controls my context.
We need better ways to fuck around: self-modifying, malleable agents.
Our product has been 100% built by agents. And it shows. Not the advertisement you think it is.
Pair with agents, don't outsource to them. Friction builds understanding and taste. This is where you actually learn.
Tools that are not predictable and reliable are detrimental to a developer's workflow, akin to a faulty hammer for a carpenter.
